title: Determine eligibility and gather required documents
description: Review if you qualify as an international graduate or skilled worker. Confirm you meet language, education, and work experience requirements for your TEER category.

title: Secure job offer from designated employer
description: Find employment with a designated Atlantic employer in your province of choice. The employer must offer you a qualifying position in an eligible TEER category.

title: Develop settlement plan with service provider
description: Work with a settlement service provider to create a settlement plan outlining your integration into Atlantic Canada.

title: Employer submits endorsement application
description: Your designated employer submits an application for provincial endorsement to the department, including your settlement plan.

title: Receive provincial endorsement certificate
description: Once approved, you receive a provincial endorsement certificate and may receive a work permit support letter if needed.

title: Apply for work permit (if required)
description: Submit a work permit application using the work permit support letter while your permanent residence application is being processed.

title: Submit permanent residence application to IRCC
description: Submit your PR application to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada along with your endorsement certificate and supporting documents.

title: IRCC reviews and approves PR application
description: IRCC processes and reviews your permanent residence application. Once approved, you can travel to Atlantic Canada to live and work.

title: Determine your permanent residence program
description: Identify which PR program you applied for (Express Entry, PNP, Quebec skilled worker, Home Child Care/Support Worker Pilot, Caring for Children/High Medical Needs, Agri-Food Pilot, or Quebec investor). This determines your specific BOWP eligibility requirements.

title: Confirm eligibility requirements
description: Verify you meet all core eligibility criteria: live in Canada (outside Quebec unless applicable), have valid or restorable work permit status, be principal applicant on PR application, have submitted complete PR application, and passed completeness check. Check program-specific requirements.

title: Gather required documents
description: Collect all supporting documents including acknowledgement of receipt letter, nomination letter (if applicable), approval in principle letter (if applicable), CSQ or permanent residence application number letter, and any documents listed in the official document checklist.

title: Prepare work permit extension application
description: Follow the official instructions for extending or changing conditions on your work permit. Select 'Open work permit' as the permit type in your application.

title: Calculate and prepare fees
description: Determine the total fees required: work permit processing fee plus open work permit holder fee. Ensure payment method is ready before submission.

title: Submit BOWP application online
description: Apply online through the official IRCC portal, uploading all required documents in designated fields (e.g., 'Client information' field for acknowledgement of receipt letter). Pay all required fees with submission.

title: Monitor application status
description: Track your BOWP application status through your online account. Ensure you remain in Canada with valid temporary resident status while awaiting a decision on your BOWP application.

title: Determine your NOC code and verify TEER level
description: Find the National Occupational Classification (NOC) code for your job and confirm it falls within TEER 0, 1, 2, or 3 categories. Ensure your role meets all skilled work experience requirements including performing lead statement actions and most main duties.

title: Verify Canadian work experience eligibility
description: Confirm you have at least 1 year of Canadian work experience (1,560 hours) gained in the 3 years before applying, while authorized to work in Canada. Document paid work only; self-employment and student work do not count.

title: Take and pass approved language tests
description: Take approved English or French language tests and achieve the minimum score in all 4 abilities: writing, reading, listening, and speaking.

title: Gather educational credentials (if applicable)
description: If you have Canadian education, gather your certificate, diploma, or degree. If you have foreign education and want to improve your rank, obtain an educational credential assessment (ECA) report for immigration purposes.

title: Confirm admissibility to Canada
description: Ensure you are admissible to Canada by verifying you have no security, criminal, or medical inadmissibility issues.

title: Decide on province or territory of residence
description: Confirm you plan to live outside Quebec (unless provincially nominated), or verify provincial nomination eligibility if applicable. Document your settlement plans.

title: Create Express Entry profile
description: Create your Express Entry profile with accurate work experience, language test scores, and education details. Do not check self-employed work if your experience qualifies under physician exemption.

title: Submit application after Invitation to Apply
description: Wait for an Invitation to Apply (ITA) and submit your full permanent residence application with all supporting documentation within the specified timeframe.

title: Complete biometrics
description: Provide fingerprints and photo at a Visa Application Centre (VAC) or Application Support Center. Required for all Express Entry applicants. Biometrics are valid for 10 years.

title: Complete medical exam
description: Attend a medical examination with an IRCC-designated panel physician. Required after submitting your e-APR. Results are valid for 12 months.

title: Receive Confirmation of Permanent Residence
description: IRCC issues your Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR). Sign and submit it, then land in Canada before the expiry date to activate your permanent residency.

title: Educational Credential Assessment
description: Have your foreign educational credentials assessed by a designated organisation such as WES so IRCC can evaluate your Canadian equivalent education level.

title: Language Testing
description: Complete an approved English or French language test (IELTS General Training or CELPIP for English; TEF Canada or TCF Canada for French) and obtain your CLB scores.

title: Create Express Entry Profile
description: Submit your Express Entry profile on the IRCC portal. Your Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score is calculated based on your age, education, work experience, and language scores.

title: Wait for Invitation to Apply
description: Your profile sits in the Express Entry pool. IRCC holds regular draws and issues Invitations to Apply (ITAs) to the highest-ranked candidates. Draw scores vary by program and economic conditions.

title: Submit Permanent Residency Application
description: After receiving your ITA you have 60 days to submit a complete online application for permanent residency. Gather all required documents, undergo medical and security checks, and pay the processing fee.

title: Determine your NOC and verify TEER eligibility
description: Find your National Occupational Classification code and confirm your job falls within TEER categories 0, 1, 2, or 3. Ensure you can demonstrate the lead statement actions and most main duties from the NOC job description.

title: Verify skilled work experience requirements
description: Confirm you have at least 1 year of continuous work (or 1,560 hours) in your primary occupation within the last 10 years. Calculate your total hours if combining part-time or multiple jobs.

title: Take approved language tests
description: Take an approved English or French language test and achieve a minimum CLB 7 in all four abilities (speaking, listening, reading, writing). Obtain official test results from an approved testing agency.

title: Obtain Educational Credential Assessment if applicable
description: If you have foreign education credentials, obtain an Educational Credential Assessment report for immigration purposes. If you have Canadian education, gather your certificate, diploma, or degree.

title: Score your selection factors and verify the 67-point minimum
description: Using the federal skilled worker points grid, calculate your score across the six selection factors: official language ability, age, education, work experience, arranged employment in Canada, and adaptability. You must reach at least 67 out of 100 to be eligible for the FSW program — falling below this threshold makes you ineligible regardless of your CRS score in the Express Entry pool.

title: Gather proof of funds if required
description: Prepare proof that you have sufficient funds for you and your family to settle in Canada, unless you are legally able to work in Canada and have a valid job offer.

title: Create and submit Express Entry profile
description: Submit your profile to the Express Entry pool with all required documents and information. Confirm your plan to settle outside Quebec unless you have a provincial nomination.

title: Await invitation to apply for permanent residence
description: Wait in the Express Entry pool for an Invitation to Apply based on your Comprehensive Ranking System score. Upon invitation, you will have a set timeframe to submit your full permanent residence application.

title: Submit e-APR within 60 days
description: Upload all required documents through the IRCC portal: passport, language results, ECA, reference letters, police certificates, proof of funds, and photos. You have exactly 60 days from your ITA to submit a complete application.

title: Complete biometrics
description: Provide fingerprints and photo at a Visa Application Centre (VAC) or Application Support Center. Biometrics are valid for 10 years.

title: Complete medical exam
description: Attend a medical examination with an IRCC-designated panel physician. Required after submitting your e-APR. Results are valid for 12 months.

title: Receive Confirmation of Permanent Residence
description: IRCC issues your COPR. Sign and submit it, then land in Canada before the expiry date.

title: Show your interest and create Express Entry profile
description: Create an online Express Entry profile in your IRCC secure account to show your interest in immigrating to Canada.

title: Confirm your NOC code is STEM-eligible
description: Check that your primary work experience NOC code falls within a qualifying STEM category (typically engineering, information technology, natural sciences, or mathematics). IRCC publishes the list of STEM-eligible NOC codes for category-based selection draws — confirm your code before building your Express Entry profile.

title: Confirm eligibility for Express Entry program
description: Ensure you meet minimum criteria and are eligible for one of the 3 Express Entry programs: Federal Skilled Worker Class, Federal Skilled Trades Class, or Canadian Experience Class.

title: Get placed in Express Entry pool
description: Once your profile meets program eligibility requirements, IRCC will place you in the Express Entry pool.

title: Receive Comprehensive Ranking System score
description: IRCC assigns you a CRS score based on your profile information. You can view your score in your IRCC account while your profile remains in the pool.

title: Wait for category-based round
description: IRCC identifies candidates eligible for specific categories and ranks profiles by CRS score. You will be ranked among eligible candidates if you meet category requirements.

title: Receive invitation to apply
description: If you are among the top-ranking eligible candidates in a category-based round, IRCC will send you an invitation to apply for permanent residence.

title: Submit permanent residence application
description: Within 60 days of receiving your invitation, submit a complete application for your chosen Express Entry program.

title: Receive decision on application
description: IRCC reviews your application based on program eligibility, profile accuracy, category eligibility, and admissibility to Canada, then makes a decision.

title: Determine eligibility as sponsor
description: Verify you meet basic requirements: at least 18 years old, Canadian citizen or permanent resident, live in Canada with primary residence in Canada, and have no disqualifying factors such as criminal convictions or outstanding financial obligations.

title: Assess family member eligibility
description: Confirm the family member you wish to sponsor meets requirements for the specific program: spouse/partner/dependent child or parents/grandparents.

title: Gather required documents
description: Collect proof of income, identification documents, and other supporting documentation as specified for your sponsorship category.

title: Complete sponsorship application forms
description: Fill out the required application forms including the undertaking and sponsorship agreement. If applicable, complete the Financial Evaluation Form (IMM 1283) to demonstrate sufficient income.

title: Submit complete application
description: Submit your application package to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) with all required documents and fees.

title: Wait for application processing
description: IRCC will process your application and may request additional information or documentation. Processing time varies based on application completeness, complexity, and current intake volumes.

title: Obtain Quebec undertaking (if applicable)
description: If you live in Quebec, submit the undertaking application to Quebec's Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration only after receiving confirmation from IRCC to do so.

title: Receive approval decision
description: IRCC issues a final decision on the sponsorship application. Upon approval, the sponsored family member can proceed with permanent residence processing.

title: Determine your National Occupational Classification (NOC)
description: Find the NOC code that matches your skilled trade job. Verify your work experience is in one of the eligible NOC groups: Major Groups 72 (excluding 726), 73, 82, 83, 92, or 93 (excluding 932), Minor Group 6320, or Unit Group 62200.

title: Verify minimum work experience requirements
description: Confirm you have at least 2 years (3,120 hours) of paid full-time work experience in your skilled trade within the 5 years before applying. Ensure you performed the lead statement actions and most main duties listed in your NOC job description.

title: Obtain job offer or certificate of qualification
description: You must have either a valid job offer for full-time employment lasting at least 1 year, or a certificate of qualification in your skilled trade from a Canadian provincial, territorial, or federal authority. Contact the appropriate provincial or territorial body governing trades to get assessed.

title: Complete language test requirement
description: Take an approved English or French language test and meet the minimum score in all 4 abilities: writing, reading, listening, and speaking.

title: Gather proof of funds or confirm employment status
description: If you do not have a valid Canadian job offer and are not legally able to work in Canada, gather documents showing you have enough money for you and your family to settle in Canada.

title: Confirm admissibility to Canada
description: Ensure you are admissible to Canada by reviewing security, criminal, and medical requirements. Gather any necessary police certificates or medical exam documentation.

title: Decide where you plan to live in Canada
description: Confirm you plan to live outside Quebec (unless you are a Provincial Nominee and must settle in the nominating province or territory). Gather proof if counting Quebec work experience.

title: Create Express Entry profile and submit application
description: Create your Express Entry profile with all required information including your NOC, work experience, language test scores, education credentials, and intended province of residence. Submit when ready.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Determine qualifying work experience
description: Review whether your work experience as a home child care provider (NOC 44100) or home support worker (NOC 44101) in a private home setting qualifies for the pilot. Confirm the work was full-time and not in an institutional setting.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Choose application category
description: Select either the Gaining Experience category if you need more work experience, or the Direct to Permanent Residence category if you already have sufficient qualifying experience.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Gather required documentation
description: Compile proof of qualifying work experience, including employment letters and work history documentation that demonstrates full-time employment in an eligible NOC code.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Create Permanent Residence Portal account
description: Set up or sign into your Permanent Residence Portal account to submit your application online.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Submit application
description: Submit your completed application through the Permanent Residence Portal before the program deadline. Note that this pilot closed on June 17, 2024.

pathway_title: Home Child Care Provider & Home Support Worker Pilots
title: Submit proof of additional work experience
description: If you applied to the Gaining Experience category and have since accumulated enough qualifying work experience, send proof of the additional experience to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

title: Determine stream eligibility
description: Use the OINP Stream Selector Tool or review program documentation to identify which of the nine OINP streams you are eligible for based on your credentials, experience, and education.

title: Employer submits job offer (if applicable)
description: Your employer registers their business in the Employer Portal and creates a job offer for your position. You will receive a job offer ID to use for registration.

title: Register expression of interest
description: Register in the OINP's expression of interest system using your job offer ID (if applicable) or directly if applying to streams that do not require a job offer. Registration must be completed within 30 calendar days of employer submission.

title: Receive invitation to apply
description: Wait for Ontario to issue an invitation to apply based on your expression of interest and the program's draw requirements. Check the OINP Program Updates page for draw details.

title: Gather required documents
description: Collect all documents specified in the document checklist for your stream, including language test results, proof of education, work experience documentation, and settlement funds evidence.

title: Submit application to OINP
description: Log into your Ontario.ca account and submit your application online within the deadline specified in your invitation (typically 14-17 calendar days). Pay the application fee at submission.

title: Receive provincial nomination decision
description: OINP reviews your application and either approves or rejects your nomination. If approved, you receive a notification.

title: Apply for permanent residence to federal government
description: Submit your application to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) using your provincial nomination. IRCC makes the final decision on permanent residence approval.

title: Verify graduation from PGWP-eligible designated learning institution
description: Confirm you completed a program at least 8 months long (or 900 hours for Quebec) at a designated learning institution (DLI) that is PGWP-eligible. Obtain official confirmation of program completion from your school.

title: Assess language requirement eligibility
description: Determine if you must meet language requirements based on your program type and application date. If you submitted your study permit application before November 1, 2024, language requirements are waived. Otherwise, arrange a language test if needed.

title: Confirm field of study eligibility (if applicable)
description: If you graduated from a college, polytechnic, or non-university program and submitted your study permit application on or after November 1, 2024, verify your field of study is on the eligible list linked to occupations in long-term shortage.

title: Gather required documents and supporting evidence
description: Collect your study permit, proof of program completion, language test results (if required), and any other documents needed to support your PGWP application.

title: Apply for PGWP within 180 days of completion
description: Submit your post-graduation work permit application within 180 days of confirmation that you completed your program of study. Ensure your study permit was valid at some point during the 180 days after graduation and before you submitted your application.

title: Pay PGWP application fee
description: Submit the PGWP application fee of $255 CAD with your application.

title: Wait for PGWP processing and decision
description: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) will review your application and notify you of the decision. Check the processing times page for current estimated wait periods.

title: Receive PGWP and begin work in Canada
description: Once approved, you will receive your post-graduation work permit. You can now legally work in Canada for the duration specified on the permit.

title: Choose a Province and Stream
description: Research provincial nomination streams that match your skills, work experience, education level, and intended destination. Each province has unique eligibility criteria and targeted occupations.

title: Submit Provincial Application
description: Apply directly to your chosen provincial government stream. If successful, you receive a Provincial Nomination Certificate (PNC) which significantly boosts your CRS score in Express Entry or allows a paper-based PR application.

title: Apply for Permanent Residency
description: Use your Provincial Nomination Certificate to apply for Canadian PR, either through Express Entry (enhanced nomination adds 600 CRS points) or the paper-based PNP stream.

title: Check eligibility requirements
description: Verify that you meet both IRCC eligibility requirements and the community-specific requirements for the participating community you are interested in.

title: Find an eligible job
description: Secure a genuine job offer with an employer in one of the 11 participating rural or northern communities that meets the community's employment criteria.

title: Submit community recommendation application
description: Submit your application for community recommendation once you have a valid job offer from an eligible employer in a participating community.

title: Receive community recommendation
description: Wait for the community to assess your candidacy based on economic fit, genuine employment opportunity, and intention to stay in the community.

title: Apply for permanent residence
description: If the community recommends you, submit your permanent residence application to IRCC for final decision on your PR status.

title: Apply for work permit (optional)
description: If eligible, submit an application for a work permit to allow you to work in Canada while your permanent residence application is being processed.

title: Obtain letter of support from designated organization
description: Contact an approved designated organization and convince them your business idea is worth supporting. The organization will assess your proposal and issue a letter of support, along with sending a commitment certificate to IRCC.

title: Verify language proficiency requirement
description: Take a language test with an approved agency and achieve Canadian Language Benchmark 5 in all bands (listening, reading, writing, speaking) in English or French.

title: Gather and prepare all required documents
description: Compile supporting documents including passport, language test results, letter of support, birth certificates, identity documents, police certificates, and proof of settlement funds. Translate and certify any documents not in English or French.

title: Create account and access PR Portal
description: Create an account or sign in to the Permanent Residence (PR) Portal. The Start-up Visa Program is called Start-Up Business Class in the portal.

title: Complete and upload application forms and documents
description: Fill out all required digital forms (IMM 0008, IMM 5669, IMM 5406, IMM 5562) and upload all supporting documents using the document checklist to ensure completeness.

title: Pay application fees online
description: Pay processing fees for yourself and any dependants, biometrics fee, right of permanent residence fee (if applicable), and any fees for medical exam and police certificates.

title: Submit application through PR Portal
description: Submit your completed application online through the PR Portal. Verify all questions are answered, fee receipt is included, and all supporting documents are uploaded. If part of a team, ensure all business partners submit their applications.

title: Respond to completeness check and requests for missing documents
description: Monitor your email for notifications from IRCC. If application is incomplete, IRCC will notify you of missing items. Fix errors and re-submit as instructed.
